When people have to hire caretakers to help elderly family members - they rely on good references. An important lesson for any business is that a satisfied customer will probably come back and they may recommend your business to a few other people. You potentially gain 2 to three more customers if you're lucky. A bad review - dissatisfied customers will tell EVERYONE about your business - you can lose 10+ potential customers. So customer satisfaction is important. That means they need to vet their employees well and follow up with customers (the families that hire caretakers).

A lot of home care operators talk to and get a business relationship with other businesses like medical equipment suppliers. Mom broke her hip and needs a walker and a caretaker - they get the walker from the medical supply store and the medical supply store gives the family your business card.

There are statistical methods for dealing with small sample sizes. If you have a small sample, but a significant effect, you can still have a statistically significant outcome. One can get a valid measurement of variance from even a n=2 sample, but the uncertainty in the true mean is quite large. That said, even with a small sample size, if the average found for Jews was 75% and for non-Jews was 5%, you would almost certainly still be well within the realm of statistical significance.
